as an annexure or schedule within an incentive and fitout deed — the works program documents the scope and chronology of the fit-out / landlord works the deed funds via incentive contributions, and underpins the deed\'s payment-milestone triggers.",\n      "condition": "When the deed funds works on a scheduled timeline and annexes a programme/Gantt/milestone schedule."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "A works_program defines the TIMING, SEQUENCE, and PHASE-LEVEL DURATIONS of construction or fitout delivery — its semantic centre is the chronological roadmap. Distinguished from: (a) `construction_works_program` — a near-identical Gantt/milestone-table concept emitted under a different label by one run (20260519-2322), kept as a distinct sibling pending Phase 3 merge adjudication (registry-flagged candidate_merge); discriminator: same artefact shape, naming convention difference only — Phase 3 likely to absorb this sibling. (b) `fitout_brief` — specifies the technical scope, materials, and physical-design requirements for fit-out works inside a single tenancy, not the chronological delivery sequence. (c) `design_brief` — specifies architectural intent, materials, structural load tolerances, and technical specifications; concerned with WHAT is built, not WHEN. (d) the key-date `milestone_table` presentation — a high-level tabular listing of key tenancy or commercial milestones (handover, rent commencement) rather than a phase-level construction Gantt with task durations — is now absorbed into this concept as a presentation variant rather than a separate sibling type (absorbed from the former milestone_table). (e) `landlord_works_schedule_subpart` (sub-component of a lease/deed) — defines the PHYSICAL SCOPE and technical tasks of landlord works, not their temporal sequencing. (f) `premises_plan` — defines spatial boundaries and floor layouts, not temporal delivery."\n}'

## Contested title

<Card id="card-t5" heading={"T-5 · eGuarantee → bank_guarantee"} tone="success" badge="PARENT_OWNS" meta={["confidence: high","title ruling"]}>

Every free-standing, on-demand financial security undertaking — whether a bank-issued Bank Guarantee / Banker's Undertaking or a specialty surety/insurer-issued Lease Bond / eGuarantee / eSecurity bond (e.g. Assetinsure, HDI Global) — routes to `bank_guarantee`. Issuer class is a field value (the 'Issuing Bank or specialty institution' field), not a type boundary.

**Why.** The self-contradiction resolves in favour of absorption: the deleted sibling sentence concedes the case ('same on-demand financial security concept … same legal function, different issuer class'), the extraction schema already captures issuer class as a field, and the rest of the graph already targets bank_guarantee for surety/insurance-backed bonds; carving out e_guarantee would fracture the ~19 acceptable_targets of contract_performance_security for zero extraction gain.

**Charitable alternatives tested.** Tested NEW_TYPE_CANDIDATE (e_guarantee as a specialty-surety issuer-class type) — ruled out because the candidate would differ from bank_guarantee on no extractable field, no relationship role, no containment shape, and no legal mechanic, only on which institution signs it (already a first-class field value); a type split with no source-side extraction need fails the taxonomy's own merge principles (cf. audit_report vs outgoings_audit_report, split precisely because scope and purpose diverge — not the case here).

<Details summary={"annual_financial_report — Annual Financial Report"}>

<Json
  title={"annual_financial_report — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "annual_financial_report",\n  "type_name": "Annual Financial Report",\n  "description": "A comprehensive formal report issued annually by a corporate entity (or consolidated corporate group) to its members, shareholders, and regulators (e.g., ASIC) providing an audited overview of the entity\'s financial performance, position, and cash flows for a fiscal year. Typically comprises a Directors\' Report, an Independent Auditor\'s Report, the core financial statements (Statement of Comprehensive Income / Profit & Loss, Statement of Financial Position / Balance Sheet, Statement of Changes in Equity, Statement of Cash Flows), and explanatory Notes to the accounts. Within property portfolios, it is used by landlords during due diligence to assess tenant or guarantor covenant strength, and is supplied by major corporate tenants as evidentiary proof of net tangible assets to satisfy lease covenants allowing self-insurance, bank guarantee waivers, or parent company guarantees.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "corporate_group_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers full statutory annual financial reports across both single-entity filings and consolidated corporate-group filings. Includes ASIC-style Australian corporate filings and equivalent foreign-jurisdiction annual reports. Encompasses variation in disclosure depth (full Directors\' Report + Auditor\'s Report + all four primary statements + Notes, versus more compact filings that omit the Cash Flow Statement or extended Notes). Covers both audited reports with unqualified opinion and those with qualified/modified audit opinions.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Reporting Entity Name, Financial Year / Reporting Period, Auditor Name, Audit Opinion Status, Director Names, Total Revenue, Net Profit (or Loss), Total Assets, Total Liabilities, Total Equity / Net Tangible Assets, Dividends Paid, Cash and Cash Equivalents, Subsidiary Entities listed, and Employee Counts.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "financial_capacity_evidence",\n      "relationship_type": "provides_evidence_for",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When the lease contains self-insurance, bank-guarantee-waiver, or parent-company-guarantee covenants conditioned on the tenant (or its corporate group) demonstrating minimum net tangible asset / balance-sheet thresholds — typically only invoked for major corporate, institutional, or anchor tenants.",\n      "purpose_description": "Supplies audited, statutory evidentiary proof of the tenant\'s (or guarantor\'s) net tangible asset value and overall balance-sheet strength, to satisfy lease covenants permitting self-insurance, the waiver of bank guarantees / security bonds, or acceptance of a parent-company guarantee in lieu of cash security.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "solvency_verification",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the lease agreement contains self-insurance, security-waiver, or parent-company-guarantee covenants whose triggers reference net tangible asset value, total equity, or audited balance-sheet metrics."\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `credit_report` (a third-party bureau risk assessment / payment-history index rather than the entity\'s own audited statement of internal financial health); distinct from `certificate_of_currency` (evidence of an external insurance policy rather than internal balance-sheet capacity to self-insure); distinct from `lease_register` (an operational asset-manager-facing report focused on portfolio rental income, not corporate financial position); distinct from `revenue_report` and `turnover_certificate` (single-property turnover or revenue reporting, not consolidated corporate financial performance); distinct from `lease_approval_submission` and other transactional credit submissions (which evaluate the merits of a prospective lease transaction rather than disclosing historical statutory corporate financials)."\n}'
  }

It is physically attached as a prefix / cover page to the front of a foreign-executed deed or agreement, certifying the signature, seal and capacity of the public official (typically a Notary Public) who executed the underlying document so that it is legally recognised in Australia without further consular legalisation. Although it sits at the front of the bundle, its substantive function is to authenticate the notary whose notarial certificate appears in the execution block of that same instrument.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_independent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Form is standardised by the Hague Convention so structural variation is narrow. The physical attachment point does not vary: every observed instance is a cover / prefix page at the FRONT of the whole foreign-executed instrument, hundreds-to-thousands of lines away from the notarial certificate (which sits in the execution block at the end). The earlier hypothesised pattern of an apostille bound directly onto the notarial certificate is NOT observed in the corpus. Label drift observed in the source corpus: one run (20260513-1638) produced the lumped label `apostille_notarial_certificate` for the same artefact, hedging the issuer clause as \'a government authority or authorized Notary Public\'; that lumped variant is absorbed here as a labelling artefact, not a distinct sub-type.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Issuing country / country of origin; name of certifying public official (typically a Notary Public); capacity / role of that official; seal / stamp identifier and authority (including notarial seal/stamp details recorded on the apostille); place of issue; date of issue; Apostille registration / certificate number; name of the issuing government department or authority.",\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `notarial_certificate` along the authentication-layer axis: an Apostille is a sovereign-government, treaty-level certificate (issued under the 1961 Hague Convention by a Ministry / Department of Foreign Affairs) authenticating the *public office and authority of the notary* who executed an underlying certification — it operates government-to-government and carries a unique treaty-metadata surface (issuing country, treaty registration number, issuing ministry). A `notarial_certificate` is the notary\'s own direct certificate operating notary-to-party, authenticating *the identity, signature, and corporate authority of the private signatories* who executed the underlying deed. Stack relationship: the apostille is one layer up from the notarial certificate (authenticator-of-the-authenticator) and would be functionless without that underlying notarial certificate. It formally appoints the Agent and defines its scope of activities (general property management, facilities management, leasing services, trust accounting and reporting), fee structure (annual management fee, leasing commissions, property accounting fees, facilities management fees), key personnel, limits of authority, insurance requirements, indemnities and compliance obligations, and empowers the Agent to procure and administer downstream service contracts and to execute and administer tenancy instruments on behalf of the Principal.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "entity_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers Property Management Agreements (property-only scope), comprehensive Asset & Facilities Management engagements (operations + facilities + leasing + reporting), and trustee/fund-level portfolio management appointments. Includes both single-property and multi-property/portfolio variants, and engagements with major institutional real-estate managers (e.g. Knight Frank, JLL). Fee mechanisms range from fixed annual management fees through to open-book cost-plus structures and percentage-based leasing commissions.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Principal/Trustee/Owner corporate details, Agent corporate details, property address or property schedule, commencement date, term and expiry, annual management fee (fixed, percentage, or open-book cost-plus), leasing commissions, property accounting / facilities management fees, key personnel, payment terms, limits of authority and delegated-authority caps, excluded activities, insurance requirements and insurable amounts, indemnity provisions, reporting requirements, and corporate-governance clauses (e.g. Modern Slavery warranties).",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "service_contract_procurement_governance",\n      "relationship_type": "governs",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "purpose_description": "Establishes the delegated authority and operating framework under which the Agent procures, executes and supervises third-party service contracts (facilities maintenance, cleaning, security, HVAC, hydraulic, electrical, fire) on the Principal\'s behalf, defining the limits-of-authority caps, excluded activities and reporting obligations that govern those procurement decisions.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "service_contract",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "portfolio_management_governance",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "tenancy_administration_authorisation",\n      "relationship_type": "authorises_agent_for",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "Applies only when the asset management agreement includes leasing/tenancy-management scope (i.e. comprehensive Asset & Facilities Management or Property Management engagements that delegate lease execution and administration). a service_contract is a downstream trade-specific procurement instrument (cleaning, security, HVAC, hydraulic, electrical, fire) executed by the Owner/Manager to engage a specialist contractor for physical works, typically procured under the authority that the asset_management_agreement establishes. Distinct from `lease_agreement`: the asset_management_agreement defines the Owner→Manager relationship and grants the Manager authority to operate the property; the lease_agreement defines the Landlord→Tenant relationship and grants the Tenant exclusive possession of premises in exchange for rent. The AMA may authorise the Manager to execute lease_agreements on the Owner\'s behalf, but the two instruments operate at different altitudes (portfolio governance vs tenancy grant) and carry different extraction profiles (management fees / limits of authority vs base rent / outgoings / security)."\n}'

    '{\n  "type_id": "bank_guarantee_checklist",\n  "type_name": "Bank Guarantee Checklist",\n  "description": "An instructional form, administrative list, or prescriptive requirements sheet (e.g. \'Bank Guarantee Checklist\', \'Requirements for Bank Guarantee\', \'Bank Guarantee Instructions\', \'Security Requirements Checklist\') provided by a landlord or their solicitor to a tenant. Lendlease LOO:302-313). bank_guarantee is a standalone root instrument, so target_parent_type_id and parent_relationship_role_id are null (Shape I); source-parent pinning is sufficient. this confirmation is a non-cashable correspondence letter that merely affirms the instrument\'s existence and validity. (2) `bank_guarantee_amendment` is a bank-issued instrument that modifies the terms of an existing guarantee (changing the expiry date, guaranteed amount, or beneficiary details); this confirmation affirms the existing terms without altering them. (3) `bank_guarantee_return_letter` is administrative correspondence that discharges, cancels, releases, or exchanges an active guarantee at the terminal phase of its lifecycle; this confirmation affirms that the guarantee is active and continuing (the opposite lifecycle phase)."\n}'

  title={"bank_statement — production entry"}

In the commercial property onboarding context, it is typically supplied by a tenant, licensee, landlord or supplier as third-party evidentiary verification of bank-account coordinates (account holder name, BSB number, account number) to support establishment of a Direct Debit Request, supplier/vendor payment setup, or other automated electronic-funds-transfer arrangement.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers bank-issued periodic statements and account-summary outputs used as third-party verification of account ownership and banking metadata in property administration. Variation observed across issuing institution (e.g. ANZ and other Australian banks) and statement format (full periodic transaction statement vs. shorter account summary), but the extractable schema is stable across variants.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Financial institution / bank name, account holder name, BSB number, account number, statement number, statement period (start and end dates), branch location, and opening / closing balance figures.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "account_details_verification",\n      "relationship_type": "provides_evidence_for",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "purpose_description": "Supplies independent third-party evidentiary proof of bank-account coordinates (account holder name, BSB number, account number) to validate the banking details captured on a downstream payment-setup instrument (Direct Debit Request or supplier/vendor onboarding form) before the automated payment mechanism is activated.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "direct_debit_request",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "account_verification",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "supplier_application_form",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "banking_details_verification",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the bank statement is supplied to support a landlord/vendor/supplier payee onboarding rather than a tenant\'s direct-debit authorisation.",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `direct_debit_request`: a bank statement is a backward-looking historical record of account activity and balances issued by the bank as a third party, whereas a Direct Debit Request is a forward-looking authorisation form executed by the account holder instructing the bank to permit recurring debits. The bank statement provides EVIDENCE OF the account; the DDR provides INSTRUCTIONS ABOUT the account. Also distinguished from payment receipts / remittance advices, which confirm a single specific completed transaction rather than summarising a period of account activity."\n}'
  }

<Details summary={"bankruptcy_search_result — Bankruptcy Search Result"}>

<Json
  title={"bankruptcy_search_result — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "bankruptcy_search_result",\n  "type_name": "Bankruptcy Search Result",\n  "description": "A formal point-in-time administrative report issued by a national personal-insolvency authority (e.g. the Australian Financial Security Authority — AFSA) recording the result of a search against the national personal insolvency index (e.g. the NPII) for a specific natural person. The report states the search criteria used (typically family name and given name(s), and where supplied, date of birth) and certifies whether any record of bankruptcy, debt agreement, personal insolvency administration or related history was matched for that individual. It is used as a due-diligence instrument to evaluate the personal solvency of proposed guarantors, directors or other natural-person signatories supporting a commercial lease.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers personal-insolvency search certificates regardless of (a) the specific national authority issuing the report (AFSA / NPII observed in the Australian sample, but the concept generalises to any equivalent national personal insolvency registry), (b) whether the result returned is \'No Matches\' / clear or one or more matched insolvency / debt-agreement / bankruptcy records, (c) whether the search criteria were limited to name fields or also included supplementary criteria such as date of birth, and (d) whether the search was run against an individual director, a personal guarantor, or another natural-person signatory. Excludes searches that target corporate entities via a corporate regulator (those belong to corporate_registry_extract).",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Searched-subject identity fields (family name, given name(s), and date of birth where supplied as a search criterion); issuing authority and index name (e.g. AFSA / NPII); search reference or order number; date (and time) the search/extract was produced; result status (e.g. \'No Matches\' / clear vs. one or more matched records); and, where matches are returned, details of the matched insolvency, debt-agreement or bankruptcy record(s).",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "individual_solvency_verification",\n      "relationship_type": "verifies",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Provides independent, certified third-party evidence of a specific natural person\'s personal-insolvency / bankruptcy status (clear or matched) drawn from the national personal-insolvency register, supporting landlord due-diligence on a director, personal guarantor, sole trader or other individual signatory in connection with a commercial lease transaction.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "solvency_verification",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `corporate_registry_extract` (and equivalent corporate-registry search artefacts) on register, subject, and field set: bankruptcy_search_result is a search against the national personal-insolvency register (AFSA / NPII in Australia) targeting a single natural person and extracting personal-identity search criteria (family name, given name(s), optional date of birth) plus a personal-insolvency match-status result; corporate_registry_extract is a search against the corporate regulator (ASIC in Australia) targeting a company / corporate entity and extracting corporate-identity fields (ACN, registered office, directors, share structure, legal standing). The two are governed by separate statutes (Bankruptcy Act 1966 vs Corporations Act 2001) and answer different due-diligence questions (personal solvency of a natural-person signatory vs corporate standing of a corporate counterparty). A combined director-and-bankruptcy pack in practice contains one instance of each, not a merged artefact."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

</Details>

Mirrors the existing lease_agreement / fitout_provision contexts; the AFL host was prose-enumerated but absent from containment_contexts."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Base Building Requirements defines the landlord\'s pre-handover engineering and services delivery thresholds (Amps, kPa, slab tolerances, HVAC targets, plumbing/fire integration) that the tenant must verify before taking possession. Internal framing note (configuration-snapshot lens absorbed from the former base_building_configuration): a single base-building services schedule can be read at either end of the lease lifecycle — as the landlord\'s pre-handover delivery threshold at commencement, and as the services-reticulation / as-installed configuration snapshot that serves as the make-good and reinstatement-audit baseline at lease end; in practice these two framings co-occur on the same Annexure-C-style schedule rather than denoting two separate documents."\n}'

tenant or developer a future option to convert the leasehold or development relationship into freehold ownership.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "agreement_to_lease",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "acquisition_right_supplement",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "grantee_security",\n      "relationship_type": "secured_by",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When the call option deed requires the Grantee to provide a financial security instrument (typically a bank guarantee) to secure the option fee, settlement obligations, or other monetary commitments arising on or following exercise of the option.",\n      "purpose_description": "Has the Grantee\'s monetary obligations under the option (option fee, settlement obligations, post-exercise commitments) protected by an unconditional on-demand financial security instrument that the Owner can draw against in the event of default.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "bank_guarantee",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "contract_performance_security",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "option_modification",\n      "relationship_type": "varied_by",\n      "necessity": "optional",\n      "purpose_description": "Has its definitions, pricing parameters, exercise window, or other operative terms updated by a subsequent bilateral deed of variation, most commonly to reflect post-execution changes to the underlying asset (e.g., building expansion changing the property definition) or to renegotiate the option\'s commercial parameters.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "deed_of_variation",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "varies_master_agreement",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `contract_of_sale`: the call option grants a contingent, unilateral right to enter the sale at a later date by the Grantee\'s election; a contract_of_sale is the binding bilateral agreement that, once executed (whether independently or on exercise of an option), effects the actual freehold transfer. The call option typically embeds an unexecuted contract_of_sale as its sale-terms annexure, but the option deed itself imposes no obligation to purchase. Distinct from `lease_agreement`: the call option grants a contingent right to acquire the freehold fee simple interest in the land; a lease_agreement grants a possessory leasehold estate (right to occupy for rent) and creates a current proprietary interest. The two instruments can coexist over the same premises (the tenure_supplement role above) but address fundamentally different legal rights — acquisition optionality versus current possession. Distinct from `agreement_to_lease`: the agreement_to_lease binds the parties to enter into a lease on satisfaction of pre-occupancy conditions (construction completion, fit-out), creating an obligation to take possession; a call option creates an optional right to acquire freehold and imposes no obligation on the Grantee to act. Distinct from `section_32_statement`: the section_32_statement is a unilateral statutory disclosure of property-level metadata authored by the Owner under the Sale of Land Act 1962 (Vic) or equivalent regime, frequently embedded inside the call option deed as an annexure; the call option deed itself is the bilateral contingent-right-grant instrument that contains the disclosure rather than the disclosure itself."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

It synthesises the asset/leasing strategy, sets out market analysis and project scope, itemises budget allowances, sensitivities (e.g. rent vs incentive trade-offs) and expected returns, and records the internal management approvals required for capital deployment.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "context_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers (a) speculative fit-out / spec-suite proposals for vacant space prior to any tenant being identified, (b) building-level capital upgrade proposals (services, base-building works), and (c) tenancy-specific capex memoranda such as make-good works or landlord-funded fit-out contributions where the works themselves are the funding subject rather than the lease commercials. Primary cohort is asset-level/speculative; tenancy-specific variants exist where the proposal funds works tied to an identified tenancy.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Project / proposal name; building name and (where applicable) level or tenancy reference; purpose of works (e.g. speculative fit-out, spec suite, make-good, upgrade); requested funding amount and budget breakdown (including $/sqm where given); project manager / sponsor; strategic rationale and market analysis; sensitivity analysis (e.g. rent vs incentive requirements, expected returns); and the schedule of internal management approvals (approval status, approvers, dates).",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "funding_authorization",\n      "relationship_type": "precedes",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When the approved capital works progress to construction execution and the contractor issues progress / SOPA payment claims that draw down against the authorised capex budget. Proposals that are approved-in-principle but not executed, or executed under a different payment mechanism (lump-sum head-contractor invoicing rather than progressive SOPA claims), do not surface this relationship.",\n      "purpose_description": "Provides the internal financial authorisation that establishes the funding envelope which downstream construction progress claims subsequently draw against.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "payment_claim",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "internal_payment_authorization",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `internal_approval_record`: Both are inward-facing landlord/fund-manager governance records, but the subject of approval differs: a `capital_expenditure_proposal` justifies asset-side capital deployment (speculative fit-outs, spec suites, building upgrades, make-good works) — frequently before any tenant is identified — and its financial model is project budget vs expected return on the asset. An `internal_approval_record` justifies the commercial variables of a specific tenant transaction (rent, incentives, lease term, deal commercials for a new lease / renewal / variation / assignment / licence) and its financial model is achieved-vs-budget rent, MAT, occupancy cost ratio, and NPV of the deal. The two often appear in sequence on the same building (capex proposal funds the spec suite; internal approval record later approves the lease that takes that suite), but they are functionally and temporally distinct governance artefacts."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

term-aligned formal car parking licence concept): casual licences are short-term or month-to-month, often issued as offer letters with short termination notice periods (e.g., 30 days) and individual vehicle plate tracking; term-aligned licences are formal multi-year deeds whose duration and review cadence mirror a specific head lease and which carry a richer relational/extraction surface (bank guarantees, levy pass-throughs, statutory CPI/market reviews). Distinguish from `licence_termination_notice`: the casual licence is a bilateral grant of parking rights, whereas the termination notice is a unilateral letter cancelling an existing parking licence (and may in fact be the instrument that terminates a casual licence). Distinguish from `pick_up_area_licence`: both are short-term throughput-oriented bay grants, but casual licences allocate bays for staff parking (vehicle plate tracked, monthly fee per bay), whereas pick-up area licences allocate bays for customer goods collection (Direct-to-Boot / Click & Collect, nominal $1.00 p.a. fee, signage and WHS traffic-control obligations, head-lease-gated termination)."\n}'

<Details summary={"caveat — Caveat"}>

<Json
  title={"caveat — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "caveat",\n  "type_name": "Caveat",\n  "description": "A formal statutory legal notice registered with a state or territory land titles office (Torrens registry) by a Caveator that forbids the registration of any subsequent dealings (such as transfers, mortgages, or further leases) against a specific property title without notice to the Caveator. It is lodged to protect an unregistered equitable interest in the land — most commonly a \'Lessee in Possession\' interest under an unregistered or long-term lease, but also covering easement grantees, equitable chargees, and other unregistered proprietary claims. The caveat carries independent legal force as a unilateral registry lock and operates as an adverse, defensive prohibition until withdrawn or lapsed.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers statutory caveats lodged under state and territory Torrens regimes to protect unregistered proprietary interests, principally lessees in possession under unregistered or long-term commercial leases (the dominant variant in this corpus), but also caveats lodged by utilities and infrastructure tenants protecting substation/equipment leases, financiers protecting equitable charges, and easement grantees protecting unregistered easement rights. Includes caveats with prohibition extents ranging from absolute (forbidding all dealings) to qualified (forbidding specific classes of dealings).",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Caveator name, Registered Proprietor name, land title reference (Volume/Folio or Torrens Title), dealing/lodgement number for the caveat itself, claimed estate or interest (e.g., Lessee, easement grantee, equitable chargee), grounds of claim (e.g., \'unregistered lease dated 21 September 1999\'), extent of prohibition (e.g., \'Absolutely\' or specific dealing classes), and Address for Service.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "equitable_interest_protection",\n      "relationship_type": "secures",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Provides statutory proprietary protection for an unregistered equitable interest in the land (most commonly a lessee-in-possession interest under an unregistered or long-term lease) by forbidding registration of any subsequent dealings on title without notice to the Caveator.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "equitable_interest_protection",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "title_dealing_restriction",\n      "relationship_type": "modifies",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Registers an encumbrance against the certificate of title\'s Torrens folio that forbids registration of further dealings (transfers, mortgages, further leases) until the caveat is withdrawn or lapses, thereby altering the registered encumbrance state of the title.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "certificate_of_title",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "registered_dealing_recordation",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "title_reference_grounding",\n      "relationship_type": "references",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "condition": null,\n      "purpose_description": "Relies on the certificate of title to identify the Registered Proprietor against whose folio the caveat operates and to fix the precise Volume/Folio (or Torrens Title) coordinates of the land being restrained. Without the title\'s state-guaranteed proprietor and folio data, the caveat lacks the identifying particulars needed to be properly lodged against the register.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "certificate_of_title",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "proprietorship_verification",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `mortgagee_consent`: a caveat is a defensive, adverse third-party prohibition lodged by a Caveator to block registration of dealings on title, whereas mortgagee_consent is an affirmative authorisation issued by a senior interest holder (typically a financial institution holding a registered mortgage) permitting a specific dealing (lease, sublease, easement, variation) to be registered. The caveat asserts a competing claim; the mortgagee_consent removes a blocking objection. Both encumber or interact with the same Torrens title but operate in opposite directions on the registrability of subsequent dealings."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

</Details>

    '{\n  "type_id": "centre_map",\n  "type_name": "Centre Map",\n  "description": "A non-scale, marketing-oriented graphical floor plan or site layout illustrating the general configuration of tenancies, shop numbering, major entry points, walkways, and common infrastructure (food courts, loading docks, carpark ramps, travelators, restrooms) within a retail shopping centre or commercial precinct. Centre maps are prepared for marketing, leasing, wayfinding, and general informational purposes; they typically carry explicit \'Not to Scale\' (NTS) disclaimers and other accuracy caveats, and they identify tenancy footprints and adjacent occupants rather than certifying technical cadastral boundaries.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "context_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers shopping-mall retail floor maps (e.g., Realserve marketing plans), building-stack diagrams, precinct-level concept maps (e.g., Barangaroo South site overviews), common-area the centre map is an uncertified, explicitly non-scale marketing/wayfinding layout that carries accuracy disclaimers and identifies adjacencies/wayfinding metadata rather than legal boundaries. Distinguishable from `fitout_design_package` — fitout design packages describe internal shop construction and finishes for a single tenancy, whereas the centre map provides centre-wide locational and adjacency context across many tenancies. Distinguishable from `subdivision_plan` — a subdivision plan defines strict legal lot boundaries within a parcel; the centre map\'s larger \'precinct master plan\' variant focuses on broader strategic/phased multi-building development layout (Stage 1A vs 1B, building footprints, road extensions) without legal-boundary force."\n}'

<Details summary={"certificate_of_title — Certificate of Title"}>

<Json
  title={"certificate_of_title — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "certificate_of_title",\n  "type_name": "Certificate of Title",\n  "description": "A formal register search statement or title certificate issued by a state or territory land registry office (e.g., Land Victoria, NSW Land Registry Services) that provides the definitive point-in-time legal status of a specific real property parcel under the Torrens system. It confirms the registered proprietor(s), describes the land parcel boundaries via legal land description (Lot/Plan, Volume/Folio), and itemises all registered encumbrances — including caveats, mortgages, easements, covenants, and registered leasehold interests.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "context_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers the full family of state land-registry title artefacts: Register Search Statements, Title Searches / Land Title Searches, Title Search Packages, and historical Certificates of Title. All variants share the same core schema (Volume/Folio, registered proprietor, land description, encumbrances) and differ only in registry-specific presentation and the depth of activity/dealings history included.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Title Reference (Volume and Folio numbers), legal land description (Lot/Plan), registered proprietor name(s), active encumbrances (caveat numbers, mortgagee details and mortgage numbers, easement references, registered leases), dealings/activity history, and the date/timestamp of the search.",\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `transfer_of_land` (and `transfer_of_land_instrument`), which are the *active* registry conveyancing instruments that effect a change in proprietorship, whereas the certificate of title is the resulting *static* public record of the current registered state. Distinct from `caveat`, which is a single defensive registry notice lodged to protect a specific unregistered equitable interest, whereas the certificate of title is the comprehensive proprietorship-and-encumbrance record on which caveats are recorded as line items. Distinct from `survey_plan`, which is the surveyor-certified spatial/cadastral measurement of the parcel (NLA/GLA/GLAR, boundary markers, measurement standard), whereas the certificate of title is the legal-tenure record — the title references the plan\'s Lot/DP identifier but does not contain the spatial measurements.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "proprietorship_verification",\n      "relationship_type": "verifies",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "purpose_description": "Provides independent state-guaranteed confirmation of the registered proprietor, Volume/Folio identifiers, and active encumbrances of the property parcel, supplying the authoritative external factual matter against which contractual parties (landlord identity in a lease, transferor identity in a transfer, registered-proprietor identity in a caveat) can be validated.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "title_registration_evidence",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "transfer_of_land",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "title_verification_dependency",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "caveat",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "title_reference_grounding",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "registered_dealing_recordation",\n      "relationship_type": "modified_by",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When a registrable dealing — a transfer of freehold, a caveat, or a registered/registrable lease — is formally lodged against the Torrens Title folio. The certificate is updated to record the new proprietor (transfer), the new encumbrance line item (caveat), or the new leasehold interest (registered lease).",\n      "purpose_description": "Records the registry-side effect of a registrable dealing on the title folio: a transfer updates the registered proprietor, a caveat adds an encumbrance/dealing-restriction line item, and a registrable lease adds a leasehold-interest line item to the title\'s encumbrance log.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "transfer_of_land",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "title_ownership_conveyance",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "caveat",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "title_dealing_restriction",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "building_management_statement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "statement_title_registration",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "land_registry_form",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "modifies_title_record",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "parcel_spatial_reference",\n      "relationship_type": "scope_defined_by",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "purpose_description": "Relies on a registered cadastral plan (Lot/DP, Lot/Plan, or analogous registered subdivision plan) to define the spatial boundaries of the parcel identified by the certificate\'s Volume/Folio. The title cites the plan\'s Lot/DP identifier as part of the land description but does not itself contain the spatial measurements.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "subdivision_plan",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "cadastral_boundary_definition",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": []\n}'
  }

<Json
  title={"change_of_control_notice — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "change_of_control_notice",\n  "type_name": "Change of Control Notice",\n  "description": "A formal notice, letter, or procedural request from a tenant to a landlord regarding a proposed change in the tenant\'s corporate control or ownership structure. It outlines the transaction (e.g., share sale), identifies the new parent entity, and may initiate the landlord\'s mandatory consent process, including associated fees and application requirements.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "tenant_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Document form varies across a formal notice, a letter, or a procedural request, each issued by the tenant to the landlord; transaction substance varies across share sales and other corporate-control changes (new parent entity identification, transaction description, expected completion date, associated consent fees, application/checklist requirements).",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Tenant Name, Landlord Name, Proposed Transaction Description, New Parent Entity, Expected Completion Date, Lease Assignment Fees, and Checklist Requirements.",\n  "sibling_discriminators": "A change_of_control_notice is the tenant-initiated request for landlord consent ahead of a corporate share/ownership transaction — its function is to TRIGGER the consent-deed workflow (and so its primary downstream artefact is consent_to_change_of_control, not the lease itself). It is structurally distinct from business_transfer_notice (post-event notification of statutory succession or franchise operator substitution that bypasses the consent workflow), from entity_transition_notice (portfolio-wide administrative/ABN-update notification following a name change or merger), and from consent_request_letter (the broader tenant correspondence form that may petition consent for any of share sale, merger, change of control, OR lease assignment — change_of_control_notice is the share/ownership-control-specific subset; where a tenant correspondence petitions consent against the dealing/change-of-control covenants specifically, this is the canonical type; where it petitions against assignment covenants or spans multiple covenant triggers, consent_request_letter applies).",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "consent_request",\n      "relationship_type": "precedes",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When the landlord requires a formal consent deed for the change-of-control transaction (i.e., when the proposed transaction triggers the lease\'s dealing/change-of-control covenants and the landlord elects to formalise consent via deed rather than waive, reject, or treat the transaction as not requiring formal consent).",\n      "purpose_description": "Establishes the tenant\'s request for landlord consent ahead of a proposed corporate-share-control transaction, providing the transaction description, new parent entity, and information the landlord needs to evaluate whether to grant consent and on what conditions.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "consent_to_change_of_control",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "consent_request_predecessor",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "notifies_lease",\n      "relationship_type": "notifies",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "condition": null,\n      "purpose_description": "Communicates to the landlord under the lease the proposed change in tenant corporate control — identifying the new parent entity, transaction structure, and expected completion — discharging the tenant\'s notification obligation under the lease\'s dealing/change-of-control covenants.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "corporate_change_notification",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": []\n}'

<Details summary={"chief_warden_manual — Chief Warden Manual"}>

<Json
  title={"chief_warden_manual — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "chief_warden_manual",\n  "type_name": "Chief Warden Manual",\n  "description": "A technical and leadership instructional sub-guide physically embedded within a building\'s master Emergency Management Manual / Plan, tailored specifically for the Chief Warden and Deputies. It details the location, mechanical function, and operational protocols of master emergency control point hardware — Fire Indicator Panel (FIP), Emergency Warning Intercommunication System (EWIS) panels, and Public Address (PA) controls — including panel key standards (e.g., 003 key switch), Auto / Manual / Isolate modes, zone-clearing buttons and indicator lights, and PA announcement scripts used during an emergency.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_dependent",\n  "document_scope": "context_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers Chief Warden / Deputy-oriented EWIS and FIP operating chapters, including PA announcement script subsections and zone-indicator reference panels. Some instances frame the content as a role-specific action checklist keyed to Alert / Evacuate tones (Emergency Control Organisation member tasks); others as a continuous technical hardware operations chapter for master control point equipment.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Master Emergency Control Point (MECP) location; Secondary Emergency Control Point (SECP) location; Fire Indicator Panel (FIP) operation status, indicator types (Break Glass, Smoke) and monitoring details; EWIS panel interface modes (Auto / Manual / Isolate); PA announcement guidelines and warning-tone descriptions (Alert / Evacuate); zone indicator meanings (Manned vs Cleared) and zone-clearing / reference button usage; cabinet and panel key standards (e.g., 003 key); tone delay settings and input indicator light logic; ECO role titles and role-specific actions on Alert / Evacuation tones.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "technical_hardware_operation_protocol",\n      "relationship_type": "supplements",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "purpose_description": "Supplies the Chief Warden / Deputies with the technical hardware-operation knowledge (FIP / EWIS / PA panel modes, keys, zone-clearing, tone controls) required to execute the tactical response procedures co-located in the parent emergency manual; tactical procedures dictate what to do, this sub-guide explains how to drive the master control point hardware to achieve it.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "emergency_response_procedures",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "operationally_supplemented_by_co_located_artefact",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "emergency_management_manual",\n      "containment_certainty": "definitive",\n      "expected_presence": "required",\n      "containment_description": "Physically embedded as a technical and leadership instructional sub-guide / chapter within the master Emergency Management Manual (also titled Emergency Management Plan or Emergency Plan in some portfolio variants — all consolidated under the single Phase-1 parent `emergency_management_manual`)."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `emergency_response_procedures` (the tactical \'what to do\' layer of hazard-coded response sequences and methodologies, RACE / PASS / Escape-Hide-Tell, Code Red / Blue / Purple / Black / Yellow / Brown): the chief_warden_manual is the technical hardware \'how to operate\' layer — it specifies the mechanical operation of FIP / EWIS / PA panels (modes, keys, zone-clearing, tone controls) and the audience is narrowed to the Chief Warden and Deputies who operate the Master Emergency Control Point. emergency_response_procedures govern human action sequences for occupants and the full Emergency Control Organisation; chief_warden_manual governs panel-and-hardware operation by command-level wardens. Both are co-located sub-guides within the same parent emergency_management_manual but address orthogonal extraction surfaces (hardware operations vs tactical action plans)."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}

"counterpart_role_id": "pre_commencement_access_supplement",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "temporary_swing_space_supplement",\n <Details summary={"commercial_deed_of_agreement — Commercial Deed of Agreement"}>

<Json
  title={"commercial_deed_of_agreement — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "commercial_deed_of_agreement",\n  "type_name": "Commercial Deed of Agreement",\n  "description": "A formal legal instrument used to record bespoke commercial arrangements between a landlord and tenant that \'touch and concern\' the land but may not be part of the primary lease term. Examples include specific covenants by the owner to provide or maintain general car parking areas or infrastructure for the public or the tenant, which terminate if the lease is terminated. Its deepest-witnessed exemplar is the anchor-tenant car-park covenant deed: a bilateral deed of covenant between a landlord/owner and a major anchor tenant (e.g. supermarket or department store) governing site-wide arrangements over the future use, redevelopment and aggregate count of car parking spaces — protecting guaranteed minimum free-space counts (e.g. 482 spaces), defining the operational impact of future development works (e.g. \'Garden Stores\', additional buildings) on the overall parking footprint, and frequently formalising related corporate reporting covenants (e.g. MAT sales records) as consideration for the protected parking capacity.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Observed variants record landlord covenants to provide or maintain general infrastructure for the benefit of a tenant or the public, with the primary witnessed example being a covenant to provide general car parking areas. Other observed shapes cover broader bespoke infrastructure/amenity guarantees that fall outside the standard lease grant. All variants share the structural feature that the deed lapses if the underlying lease is terminated. The car-park-covenant variant (absorbed from the former car_park_agreement) covers specialised, high-altitude site-parking deeds negotiated between institutional landlords and tier-1 anchor tenants, ranging from pure parking-capacity covenants (aggregate minimum space counts, redevelopment-impact logic) through to broader \'property use\' / \'carpark\' deeds that also bundle ancillary corporate reporting covenants such as MAT (Moving Annual Turnover) sales records as consideration for the protected parking provision.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Parties, Lot references, Specific Covenant details (e.g., \'provide X car spaces\'), Duration/Term linked to the lease, and Successorship terms. For car-park covenant deeds specifically (absorbed from the former car_park_agreement): transacting parties; centre / property / premises identification (including Lot Numbers and any Hatched Area ID); total guaranteed car space count (e.g. 482 free spaces); aggregate site-wide capacity thresholds; redevelopment terms and impact logic for future precinct alterations (e.g. Garden Stores, additional buildings); lease linkage and termination triggers tied to the head/anchor lease; and MAT sales-record reporting mandates where present.",\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Unlike `car_parking_licence`, which grants a tenant the non-exclusive right to USE specific parking spots, this deed represents a covenant by the owner to PROVIDE or MAINTAIN general areas/infrastructure. Unlike `lease_agreement`, it does not grant exclusive proprietary tenure over premises — it records a free-standing covenant running with the land that supplements the lease. Distinguished from `car_park_lease_agreement` because this instrument does NOT grant any estate in land over the car park: it is a bilateral deed of covenant attaching obligations (capacity, redevelopment, reporting) to the landlord and to the anchor tenant in support of the anchor\'s separate head lease, whereas a `car_park_lease_agreement` is a primary lease granting the lessee exclusive possession of the car-park premises themselves. Internal-exemplar note (absorbed from the former car_park_agreement): the narrower anchor-tenant car-park covenant deed — site-wide parking capacity, guaranteed minimum free-space counts, redevelopment-impact restrictions, and MAT corporate-reporting covenants — is the deepest-witnessed instance of this concept, held here as a sub-variant rather than as a separate type (a future split would re-extract it; see MERGE_DECISIONS_LOG.md).",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "commercial_arrangement_supplement",\n      "relationship_type": "supplements",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Adds bespoke commercial arrangements (e.g., landlord covenants to provide or maintain general car parking or infrastructure) that operate alongside a primary lease without altering its standard terms, and that lapse if the lease is terminated. In its witnessed car-park-covenant form this adds bilateral site-wide parking covenants — guaranteed minimum free-space counts, redevelopment-impact restrictions, and (where present) MAT corporate reporting obligations — whose lifespan is contractually tied to the major anchor tenant\'s primary leasehold tenancy of the centre (absorbed from the former car_park_agreement.primary_tenancy_parking_covenants role: 5/5-run convergent, required, head-lease termination linkage per File 16 Clause 5).",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "bespoke_collateral_supplement",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": []\n}'

<Details summary={"company_registration_certificate — Company Registration Certificate"}>

<Json
  title={"company_registration_certificate — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "company_registration_certificate",\n  "type_name": "Company Registration Certificate",\n  "description": "A formal, free-standing statutory certificate issued by a national corporate regulator (e.g., ASIC in Australia) that certifies a specific corporate-lifecycle event in respect of one legal entity — typically the initial registration (incorporation) of a company, the registration of a foreign company, or the registration of a change of company name. The certificate is the definitive primary decree of the event: it records the regulator\'s seal/commissioner details, the company\'s ACN/ABN, the previous and new name where applicable, and the effective date. In commercial leasing it is used to evidence the legal identity (and identity continuity) of a corporate counterparty — most commonly to bridge a legacy tenant name on an existing lease to the current trading entity following rebranding or restructure, so that the chain of tenure can be maintained without triggering a formal assignment.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "entity_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers Certificates of Registration of a Company (initial incorporation), Certificates of Registration on Change of Name, and Certificates of Registration of a Foreign Company. All variants share the same statutory-certificate shape (regulator-issued, single event, fixed effective date) and differ only in which lifecycle event is being certified.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Current company name; former company name (for change-of-name variants); ACN and/or ABN; effective date of registration or change of name; date of issue; registration state / jurisdiction; type of company; issuing authority and regulator seal / commissioner details; certificate number.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "corporate_identity_verification",\n      "relationship_type": "verifies",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "Authored when a corporate tenant counterparty has undergone a change of name, has been recently incorporated, or is a foreign-registered company, and statutory proof of the lifecycle event is required to confirm legal identity continuity on the lease.",\n      "purpose_description": "Independently confirms the legal registration (and, where applicable, the name-change history) of a corporate party named on the lease, providing the regulator-certified evidence required to align legacy lease records with the current trading entity without triggering a formal assignment.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "corporate_identity_verification",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the tenant or another corporate party named on the lease has undergone a name change, has been recently incorporated, or is a foreign-registered company requiring identity verification."\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `corporate_registry_extract` on three substantive axes consistently called out by every SE entity: (a) temporal shape — the certificate is a one-time STATIC decree fixed to the date of a single lifecycle event (incorporation, change of name, foreign-company registration), whereas the extract is a DYNAMIC point-in-time snapshot of the company\'s live register that ages out as soon as officers, share capital, or addresses change; (b) authoring posture — the certificate is a primary regulatory instrument issued by ASIC at the moment of the certified event, whereas the extract is an administrative database read produced on demand by ASIC or authorised third-party search platforms (InfoTrack, Dye & Durham); (c) extractable schema — the certificate carries a small, fixed field set (former/new name, ACN, effective date, regulator seal) targeted at proving the lifecycle event, whereas the extract carries the full company-register payload (officers, share classes, UHC, registered office, lodgment history) targeted at KYC and Section 127 signatory verification. The two are complementary: a tenant onboarding pack may carry both, but they answer different questions and are NOT substitutes."\n}'
  }

    '{\n  "type_id": "conditions_for_contractors",\n  "type_name": "Conditions for Contractors",\n  "description": "A technical schedule physically integrated within a lease agreement that defines the mandatory health, safety, and environmental obligations for third-party contractors and sub-contractors performing fit-out or alteration works on the leased premises. It covers coordination of industrial matters, specific structural prohibitions (e.g., drilling structural members), waste/rubbish removal duties, and landlord indemnities against contractor delay claims.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_dependent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Observed exclusively as a technical schedule embedded within a lease agreement. Presence within a given lease is conditional on the lease anticipating significant tenant fit-out or alteration works.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Contractor health/safety/environmental obligations; coordination-of-industrial-matters provisions; permit requirements; specific structural prohibitions; waste/rubbish removal duties; landlord indemnities against contractor delay claims.",\n  "relationship_roles": [],\n  "containment_contexts": [\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n      "containment_certainty": "definitive",\n      "expected_presence": "conditional",\n      "condition": "Present when the lease anticipates or permits significant tenant fit-out, alteration, or structural works on the premises.",\n      "containment_description": "A technical safety schedule physically integrated as an annexure within the master lease agreement, regulating the tenant\'s contractors during the construction phase the parent lease permits."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `contractor_site_safety_rules`: this concept is a technical schedule physically embedded within a single lease_agreement, authored bespoke to that lease, and binds the tenant\'s own builders during a defined one-off fit-out or alteration works phase that the lease itself permits. `contractor_site_safety_rules` (the CE) is a portfolio-standard / building-wide standing policy document (e.g. Knight Frank DOC0861 \'AMS Contractor Site Safety Rules\') typically embedded within service_contracts to govern the landlord-side service-provider and maintenance-contractor population on an ongoing basis. Discriminating axes: (i) parent document — lease_agreement vs service_contract (CE may also surface within a lease package in rare cases, but its identity is the standing policy artefact, not the lease-bespoke schedule); (ii) governed population — tenant\'s nominated fit-out builders vs landlord\'s standing contractor panel; (iii) temporal scope — one-off fit-out/construction window vs ongoing operations; (iv) authorship/provenance — drafted into the individual lease vs portfolio policy attached unchanged across many parents. Also distinguished from generic `lease_rules` / house_rules, which govern occupant daily behaviour rather than contractor construction-phase HSE compliance."\n}'

<Details summary={"conditions_precedent_schedule — Conditions Precedent Schedule"}>

<Json
  title={"conditions_precedent_schedule — production entry"}

    '{\n  "type_id": "conditions_precedent_schedule",\n  "type_name": "Conditions Precedent Schedule",\n  "description": "A schedule or operative clause embedded in a host instrument — most commonly a deed (surrender, incentive/fitout, works, or side deed) and sometimes directly in a lease body — defining the specific events, approvals, works completions, or dependency conditions (such as execution of another linked lease, gaining vacant possession of a site, completion of refurbishment, FIRB or statutory/licensing clearance, or surrender by an outgoing tenant) that must be satisfied before the host instrument (or specified obligations within it) becomes legally effective and operative.   json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "confined_space_register",\n  "type_name": "Confined Space Register",\n  "description": "A comprehensive building-level Work Health and Safety (WHS) compliance and risk-management document that identifies, locates, and registers every enclosed or partially enclosed space on a property meeting the statutory definition of a \'confined space\' (e.g. stormwater and drainage pits, grease traps, fire-water / sprinkler tanks, sewer retention sumps, plenum tunnels, shafts, voids). The register serves as the master site hazard inventory: it documents the assessment methodology (typically a four-part statutory criteria checklist A–D plus atmospheric / oxygen / engulfment factors), provides a tabulated register of identified spaces with photographic evidence, assigns risk ratings (likelihood × consequence), and mandates site-wide operational controls including permit-to-work systems, rescue plans, atmospheric monitoring, energy isolation, standby-person requirements, and contractor access protocols (e.g. SINE).",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "context_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers Confined Space Registers, Confined Space Reference Documents, Confined Space Audits & Registers (consultant-issued — e.g. AESC, Stokes Safety, WSP — and landlord-issued internal formats), photo-based hazard maps, and physical-hazard Property/Safety Risk Registers whose primary content is the confined-space inventory (the May-13 \'safety_risk_register\' variant). All variants apply a consistent statutory evaluation framework (Criteria A–D, oxygen, engulfment) to physical site volumes and prescribe operational access controls.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Property address and BCA (Building Code of Australia) classification; audit / inspection date; auditor name and credentials; building manager status; total count of registered confined spaces; master asset summary table (Space ID / Risk Reference ID, asset description, location); per-asset hazard type (grease trap, sprinkler tank, sewer pit, stormwater drain, etc.); statutory risk factors (Criteria A–D, atmospheric / oxygen / biological / engulfment); risk level (high / medium / low, inherent vs residual); required control measures (signage, entry permit, rescue plan, standby person, lock-box, atmospheric monitoring); site-wide access policies (SINE contractor system, permit-to-work rules); and photographic evidence index.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "hazard_baseline_input",\n      "relationship_type": "informs",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When the consuming downstream artefact has scope that touches confined-space-relevant assets (sprinkler tanks / fire-water tanks for AFSS; emergency-plan hazard baselines for the emergency management manual; trade scope covering pit/tank/drain work for a service contract). Many AFSS, emergency manuals, and service contracts have no such scope overlap and do not consume the register.",\n      "purpose_description": "Provides the building\'s authoritative inventory of confined-space hazards and required entry controls as baseline input to downstream safety-compliance instruments and operational service agreements that must account for those hazards in their certifications, planning, or contracted scope.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "annual_fire_safety_statement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "hazard_inventory_basis",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "emergency_management_manual",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "hazard_baseline_input",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "service_contract",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "hazard_baseline_input",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `confined_space_assessment` (its CE granular-leaf child): the register is the master site-wide manifest — building BCA classification, total asset count, methodology preamble, site-wide entry-control policy (SINE protocols, permit-to-work systems, rescue plans), and the tabulated index of identified spaces — while the assessment is the per-asset technical risk-evaluation sheet for a single pit/tank/grease trap (Criteria A–D checklist results, per-asset hazard inventory, risk score, asset-specific control prescriptions, identification photograph). Distinguished from material-hazard registers (asbestos register, hazardous materials register) which catalogue chemical/material composition and asbestos-bearing fabric rather than physical enclosure volumes. Distinguished from broader property risk assessments which evaluate all site risk types (traffic, slip, security, environmental) at portfolio-overview level rather than the confined-space-specific WHS statutory-criteria framework. Distinguished from technical inspection / service / thermographic reports which record active maintenance and testing events rather than identifying and classifying the underlying static hazard volumes."\n}'

    '{\n  "type_id": "consent_request_letter",\n  "type_name": "Consent Request Letter",\n  "description": "A formal written communication issued by a tenant (or its legal representatives) to a landlord providing notice of an anticipated corporate transaction — typically a share sale, merger, or other change of control — and petitioning the landlord for formal consent pursuant to the lease\'s \'Dealing\' / change-of-control / assignment covenants. The letter outlines the proposed transaction (parties, anticipated completion date, regulatory clearances), enumerates the affected leases across the tenant\'s portfolio, sets a response deadline, and frequently includes a counter-signature block by which the landlord can grant irrevocable conditional consent on the face of the request, optionally accompanied by requested waivers of specific landlord rights. It is the procedural trigger that initiates the consent workflow culminating in the executed Deed / Consent to Change of Control.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Encompasses tenant-issued consent request letters for share sales, corporate mergers, internal group restructures, and other change-of-control / deemed-assignment events; covers letters petitioning a single landlord under one named lease and letters petitioning a landlord (or landlord group) under multiple affected leases across a portfolio (umbrella consent requests); covers both plain-form notice-and-request letters and letters incorporating a landlord counter-signature block intended to operate as the executed consent instrument when countersigned. Also covers tenant requests for collateral waivers of landlord rights (e.g., waiver of deemed-assignment treatment) issued alongside the consent petition.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Petitioning Tenant identity (and any legal-representative author); Landlord identity (and Landlord Group identifier where the request spans multiple landlord entities); Proposed Transaction description (share sale / merger / corporate restructure / parent acquisition; named acquiring entity where disclosed); Anticipated Completion / Effective Date; list of Affected Leases across the portfolio (with shop / suite / centre identifiers); specific lease clauses triggered (Dealing / Change of Control / Assignment covenant references); response deadline imposed on the landlord; requested waivers of specific landlord rights; counter-signature block (where present) and the form of consent the landlord is asked to grant.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "petitions_consent_for",\n      "relationship_type": "precedes",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Formally petitions the landlord to grant consent to an anticipated corporate transaction (share sale, merger, change of control) under the lease\'s dealing covenants, supplying transaction details and effective date and initiating the procedural timeline that culminates in the executed Consent to Change of Control instrument.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "consent_to_change_of_control",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "consent_request_predecessor",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `consent_to_change_of_control` (the terminal executed legal instrument granting the landlord\'s consent — this letter is the inbound tenant petition initiating the workflow, not the executed authorisation closing it).
