    '{\n  "type_id": "contract_of_sale",\n  "type_name": "Contract of Sale",\n  "description": "A formal, binding bilateral contract between a Vendor and a Purchaser for the sale and transfer of real property (freehold estate), establishing the purchase price, deposit amount, settlement period, particulars of sale, general conditions, and special conditions governing the transaction. In leasing portfolios it typically appears in one of two shapes: (a) an executed standalone contract effecting the freehold transfer, or (b) an unexecuted pro-forma / template annexed to a Call Option deed, ready to bind the parties upon exercise of the option.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_independent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Two physical-embedding shapes are attested across runs: (1) an unexecuted pro-forma / template Contract of Sale annexed to a Call Option deed (the dominant shape in this leasing corpus — 5 of 6 runs author a call_option / call_option_deed containment context); (2) a standalone executed Contract of Sale (attested by the 20260513-1638 run, which authored no containment context and classified as standalone). Substantive content variance includes whether the contract is annotated as \'subject to lease\', whether GST treatment uses the Going Concern exemption or Margin Scheme, and whether trust liability caps apply.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Vendor and Purchaser identities; property address and land identifiers (Lot/Plan, Volume/Folio); purchase price; deposit amount and/or percentage; balance due; settlement date and/or settlement period; particulars of sale; general conditions; special conditions; GST status (including Going Concern and Margin Scheme treatments); \'subject to lease\' / tenant-in-possession encumbrance status; and trust liability caps where applicable.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "statutory_vendor_disclosure",\n      "relationship_type": "requires_evidence_from",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Mandates that the Vendor furnish the statutory pre-contract disclosure statement covering title, registered encumbrances (easements, covenants, Section 173 agreements), planning zones and overlays, outgoings, and related property-level statutory matters required by the governing real-property legislation before the contract can be validly signed or settled.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "section_32_statement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "statutory_vendor_disclosure",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "call_option",\n      "containment_certainty": "contextual",\n      "expected_presence": "conditional",\n      "condition": "Present when the contract is bound into a Call Option deed as a pre-agreed unexecuted pro-forma annexure (the dominant shape in this leasing portfolio); absent when the contract is executed and stands as a freehold-transfer instrument in its own right (the standalone variant).",\n      "containment_description": "An unexecuted pro-forma / template Contract of Sale physically annexed to a Call Option deed (typically as \'Attachment 1\' or a master schedule), pre-agreed by the parties so that the executed contract is ready to bind both sides immediately upon exercise of the call option."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `lease_agreement` because the Contract of Sale transfers the fee simple (ownership) interest in the property rather than granting a tenancy / right of usage — the extractable surface is dominated by purchase price, deposit, and settlement mechanics rather than rent, term, and tenancy covenants. Distinct from `call_option_deed` because the Contract of Sale is a binding bilateral obligation to buy and sell that effects the transfer, whereas a Call Option deed grants only a contingent unilateral right to require the counterparty to enter the sale — in this corpus the two concepts are often co-located (the Contract of Sale is the unexecuted pro-forma bound into the Call Option deed) but they remain functionally separate instruments with distinct extractable surfaces and distinct legal effect."\n}'

Distinct from `safety_policy_provisions` (which is a narrower safety-protocols schedule embedded within telecommunications licence agreements covering specific high-risk access tasks at sub-component altitude; this concept is the comprehensive portfolio-wide contractor WHS framework governing prequalification, induction and the full permit-to-work suite). Also distinguished from non-judicial instruments at adjacent altitudes: from a settlement agreement (a contractual deed negotiated between private parties — the court order is a regulatory instrument issued by the judiciary, not a negotiated contract); from a statutory declaration (a sworn first-person statement of facts — the court order compels action, the declaration evidences facts); from a land registry request or other party-issued administrative form (the court order is judicially issued and authenticated by seal/signatory; an administrative form is party-issued to update a public register)."\n}'

The hazardous_materials_register tracks STATIC building-fabric hazards (asbestos, lead paint, synthetic mineral fibres integrated into the structure). Extraction schemas are disjoint: UN numbers and L/kg volumetric limits for DG; building-location and remediation-status for HM. Distinguished from `confined_space_register`: The dangerous_goods_register catalogues CHEMICAL SUBSTANCES stored within a space (substance-keyed). The confined_space_register catalogues PHYSICAL VOIDS within the building that present entry/atmosphere risks (location-keyed). Different subject domain, different safety regime. Distinguished from `lease_rules`: The dangerous_goods_register is a QUANTITATIVE TECHNICAL INVENTORY (chemicals × quantities × classes) defining the boundaries of permitted chemical use. The lease_rules document is BEHAVIOURAL CONDUCT PROTOCOL (tenant conduct, hours, common-area use). The DG register is consumable by fire-safety systems and insurers; lease_rules are consumable by property managers enforcing tenant behaviour."\n}'

<Details summary={"deed_of_consent_to_sublease — Deed of Consent to Sublease"}>

<Json
  title={"deed_of_consent_to_sublease — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "deed_of_consent_to_sublease",\n  "type_name": "Deed of Consent to Sublease",\n  "description": "A formal tripartite legal deed executed between a head landlord (owner), a tenant (sublessor), and a subtenant (sublessee) by which the landlord grants the contractually required consent for the tenant to sublet all or part of the demised premises. It establishes the subtenant\'s direct compliance obligations to the landlord, preserves the landlord\'s rights under the head lease, and typically includes a \'Redirection of Rent\' / \'Redirection Notice\' mechanism allowing the landlord to collect rent directly from the subtenant if the head tenant defaults. The consent is contingent on the continued validity and primacy of the head lease. The deed establishes privity of contract between the new owner and the tenant from a specified Settlement/Assignment Date and frequently records trustee limitation-of-liability terms for the incoming purchaser. <Details summary={"deed_of_novation — Deed of Novation"}>

<Json
  title={"deed_of_novation — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "deed_of_novation",\n  "type_name": "Deed of Novation",\n  "description": "A formal tripartite legal deed in which a substitute party replaces a retiring party under an existing ancillary or pre-occupancy contract (most commonly an Agreement to Lease or an Incentive and Fitout Deed) with the consent of the continuing party (typically the tenant). The deed transfers all future rights, obligations, and liabilities to the substitute party while releasing the retiring party from future performance, and is legally distinct from an assignment (which transfers an interest under an existing contract) and a variation (which amends terms while the parties remain the same) — it extinguishes the original contract and creates a fresh contract on identical terms between the new line-up of parties. In commercial property portfolios it is the standard mechanism used during building sales to transfer the developer/vendor\'s outstanding pre-occupancy and side-deed obligations to the new owner, frequently with explicit carve-outs preserving the retiring party\'s accrued historical liabilities and (where the substitute party is a trustee) trustee-entity liability limitations.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers Deeds of Novation (and synonymous Novation Deeds / Novation Agreements) for Incentive and Fitout Deeds, Agreements to Lease (AFLs), and other ancillary developer-contract handovers. Typically triggered by asset sales / building divestments where the vendor\'s outstanding pre-occupancy or side-deed obligations are transferred to the incoming purchaser.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Retiring Party, Substitute Party, Continuing Party; Effective Date of the novation; reference to the novated underlying contract (instrument name and original execution date — e.g. AFL, Incentive Deed); release-of-liability and indemnity provisions; past-liability carve-outs preserving accrued historical claims against the retiring party; and trustee-entity liability limitations where the substitute party is a trustee.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "tripartite_party_substitution",\n      "relationship_type": "novates",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Substitutes a retiring party with a substitute party under the referenced ancillary or pre-occupancy contract, with the continuing party\'s consent — releasing the retiring party from future performance, binding the substitute party on identical terms, and extinguishing the original contract in favour of a fresh tripartite contract on the same terms.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "incentive_and_fitout_deed",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "party_substitution",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the underlying contract being novated is an incentive and fitout deed (typically on building sale / landlord change of control).",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "agreement_to_lease",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "party_substitution",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the underlying contract being novated is an agreement to lease (typically on pre-completion sale of the development asset, transferring developer obligations to the incoming owner).",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "party_novation",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `deed_of_covenant`, which has an incoming party (typically a new owner) assume the active covenants of the primary lease itself — covenant assumption layered on top of the existing contract, not party substitution. Distinguished from `deed_of_assignment` (assignment of lease / assignment of contract), which transfers an existing interest while the original contract continues — assignment leaves the contract intact and substitutes the holder of an interest, whereas novation extinguishes the contract and creates a new one between a new party line-up. Distinguished from a lease or contract variation (e.g. variation_of_lease), which amends terms while keeping the parties the same. Distinguished from an attornment / attornment notice, which is a unilateral administrative notice acknowledging a new landlord rather than a tripartite substitution with retiring-party release. Distinguished from a deed of consent, which records the continuing party\'s consent without itself effecting the substitution — a novation deed both records consent and performs the substitution."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

claims) and from a Deed of Surrender (which terminates the lease and ends the tenure relationship rather than preserving it). The lease survives, modified in extent — contrast whole-estate surrender, which terminates it.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "partially_surrendered_by",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the surrender covers part only of the demise and the lease continues over the balance.",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "A Deed of Surrender is a freestanding bilateral exit deed that ends an existing leasehold estate before expiry. It is distinct from `surrender_of_licence`, which ends a non-exclusive licence and focuses on asset removal or licence-specific make-good rather than lease/title clearance; from `surrender_provision`, which is an embedded clause or schedule in a successor lease or AFL rather than a separate instrument; from `lease_agreement`, which grants the estate being surrendered; from `deed_of_variation`, which amends an ongoing lease without extinguishing it; and from `notice_to_vacate`, which is unilateral departure notice rather than the bilateral legal act of surrender."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

The master agreement is most commonly a lease, but also an agreement for lease, a non-exclusive contractual licence (telecommunications, car-parking, storage, digital media, signage, service connection, or general ancillary), or a call option deed. The instrument references a named prior agreement, fixes an effective date, and substitutes new wording / durations / figures for existing ones — recording bilateral changes such as term extensions and option-exercise renewals, rent resets and review-method changes, area expansions or partial surrenders, updated reference-schedule items, substituted definitions, replacement security amounts, added or deleted operational covenants, updated licensee/grantee entity details, and replacement technical equipment plans — while preserving the validity and chain of title of the original instrument it varies. Where the parent interest is a registered lease, the deed is often lodged through a statutory registry shell (e.g. NSW Form 07VL, QLD Form 13, ACT Form 022-VSL); the registry form is the wrapper, the deed is the substantive contract.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Generic Deeds of Variation (covering rent resets, area changes, covenant updates); Lease Extension Deeds and Deeds of Extension and Variation (including South Australian Form E2 Extensions of Lease); Deeds of Renewal, Renewal-and-Variation Deeds, and Renewal of Licence Agreements (formalising the exercise of a contractual option for a further term); <Details summary={"deferred_rent_provision — Deferred Rent Provision"}>

<Json
  title={"deferred_rent_provision — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "deferred_rent_provision",\n  "type_name": "Deferred Rent Provision",\n  "description": "An embedded clausal sub-schedule or structural sub-part — physically integrated within a lease agreement, a deed of variation, or a variation table — that establishes a structured repayment plan for a specific sum of rental debt deferred from a prior period. It identifies the Deferred Rental Amount, coordinates the schedule of instalment dates and amounts (the Deferral Repayment Period), and establishes default/acceleration triggers for immediate repayment of the outstanding balance.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_dependent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers the observed shapes of deferred-rent repayment plans: (a) provisions inserted via a variation_table in a deed of variation negotiated mid-term (typically following pandemic-era or other disruption-driven arrears accumulation), and (b) provisions written directly into the lease or its variation schedules. Within either host, the schedule may use monthly or quarterly instalments and may or may not include explicit default/acceleration triggers tied to non-payment of any single instalment.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Total Deferred Rental Amount; number of repayment instalments; instalment amounts (monthly or quarterly); instalment due dates / Deferral Repayment Period; and acceleration/default clausal triggers (e.g., entire outstanding balance becomes immediately payable on default of any single instalment).",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "arrears_instalment_structure",\n      "relationship_type": "modifies",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Restructures the parent lease\'s financial obligations by deferring a defined historical rent debt into a structured instalment plan with explicit due dates, instalment amounts, and default-acceleration triggers.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "temporary_financial_concession",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "variation_table",\n      "containment_certainty": "definitive",\n      "expected_presence": "conditional",\n      "condition": "Present when rent from a prior period has been deferred and the parties have structured the recovery into a defined instalment plan (most commonly negotiated mid-term following pandemic-era or other disruption-driven arrears accumulation).",\n      "containment_description": "A structural sub-part — typically a clausal sub-schedule or sub-section — physically embedded within a variation_table that itself sits inside a deed_of_variation or a variation schedule of the lease, establishing the instalment plan for the deferred rental sum."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguishable from `rent_reduction_schedule` (also an embedded rent-modifying schedule, but manages PROSPECTIVE rent concessions — rent-free periods, annual caps, percentage reductions over a defined concession window — rather than the RETROSPECTIVE recovery of already-accrued debt); from `rent_relief_deed` (a STANDALONE bilateral deed granting temporary waivers or forbearance, whereas this is an EMBEDDED clause setting up a structured repayment plan, not a waiver); and from a generic `repayment_schedule` (which typically manages the clawback of landlord inducements or fit-out contributions on early lease termination, not the repayment of historical base-rent arrears)."\n}'

<Details summary={"demolition_notice — Demolition Notice"}>

<Json
  title={"demolition_notice — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "demolition_notice",\n  "type_name": "Demolition Notice",\n  "description": "A formal statutory or contractual notice issued by a landlord to a tenant pursuant to the demolition or redevelopment break covenants of a lease (e.g., Clause 26). It notifies the tenant of the landlord\'s active intention to demolish or substantially renovate the building, legally mandates vacant possession by a firm \'Termination Day\', and outlines the tenant\'s statutory rights to compensation or early surrender. The notice typically annexes graphical redevelopment or demolition plans defining the spatial extent of the works.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Encompasses Formal Demolition Notices, Demolition Termination Notices, Landlord Notices of Demolition, and Notices of Termination due to Redevelopment.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Lessor and Lessee identifiers, Premises reference, Lease reference, Notice Date, Termination Day (vacate date), Demolition / Redevelopment Works description, Compensation rights and statutory early-surrender options, and specified notice periods.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "redevelopment_termination",\n      "relationship_type": "terminates",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Unilaterally brings the lease to a definitive end pursuant to redevelopment or demolition break covenants, mandating vacant possession by the stated Termination Day to clear the site for substantial building works.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "tenancy_termination",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "redevelopment_briefing_predecessor",\n      "relationship_type": "follows",\n      "necessity": "conditional",\n      "condition": "Where the demolition has been foreshadowed by a prior informational redevelopment notice covering the same project; many demolition notices are issued without an antecedent informational precursor.",\n      "purpose_description": "Records that the formal statutory demolition mandate is the legal escalation of an earlier informational redevelopment briefing for the same project, establishing chronological lineage from project announcement to binding termination.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "redevelopment_notice",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "redevelopment_informational_briefing",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguishable from `redevelopment_notice` because the demolition notice is a binding legal mandate that terminates the leasehold estate, whereas a redevelopment notice is an informational update on project staging or building upgrades that does not by itself end the tenancy. Distinguishable from `notice_to_vacate` on directionality and exercising party: the demolition notice is landlord-issued and unilaterally terminates the tenant\'s interest pursuant to landlord redevelopment break rights, whereas a notice to vacate is tenant-issued and communicates the tenant\'s intention to surrender / cease trading. Distinguishable from `lease_expiry_notice` because the demolition notice exercises an early-termination break right triggered by landlord redevelopment intent (compensation entitlements typically attach), whereas a lease expiry notice records the natural end-of-term date with no compensation trigger."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

It itemises landlord-funded fit-out assets, building services, and capital works — specifying acquisition cost, effective life, depreciation rate (Prime Cost vs Diminishing Value), and written-down value — allocating costs into Division 40 (Plant & Equipment) and Division 43 (Capital Works / Building Write-off). It is the definitive record for allocating tax benefits and ownership of fit-out components between landlord and tenant under Australian tax legislation.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_independent",\n  "document_scope": "tenant_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers Depreciation Schedules, Capital Allowance Schedules, and Capital Works Tax Depreciation Reports authored by Quantity Surveyors or tax specialists. Variant features include Division 40 (Plant & Equipment) versus Division 43 (Capital Works) allocations and Prime Cost versus Diminishing Value depreciation methods.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Report date and issuing Quantity Surveyor firm details; total landlord contribution / total installed capitalised fit-out cost; itemised asset categories (e.g. joinery, painting, floor coverings, HVAC and other building services); per-asset acquisition date and acquisition/installed cost; Division 40 vs Division 43 allocation; tax effective life (years); depreciation rate and method (Prime Cost vs Diminishing Value); annual deduction schedules and written-down value (WDV) profiles across multiple tax years.",\n  "relationship_roles": [],\n  "containment_contexts": [\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n      "containment_certainty": "contextual",\n      "expected_presence": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When the lease includes (or memorialises) landlord-funded fit-out works for which capital-allowance documentation is required to allocate tax benefits and ownership between landlord and tenant.",\n      "containment_description": "A Quantity Surveyor-authored technical tax and accounting schedule physically bound as an annexure to a lease agreement, itemising landlord-funded fit-out assets and their depreciation parameters (Division 40/43, Prime Cost/Diminishing Value, effective life, WDV)."\n    },\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "incentive_and_fitout_deed",\n      "containment_certainty": "contextual",\n      "expected_presence": "conditional",\n      "condition": "When the landlord\'s incentive/fitout contribution is documented via a separate side deed and requires formal tax apportionment and ownership demarcation for the capital assets funded.",\n      "containment_description": "A Quantity Surveyor-authored technical tax and accounting schedule physically bound as an annexure to an incentive (and fitout) deed, itemising the assets funded by the landlord\'s capital contribution and their depreciation parameters."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "A `depreciation_schedule` is a FINANCIAL/TAX record: it carries Quantity Surveyor-authored capital-allowance metadata (Division 40 vs Division 43 allocations, Prime Cost vs Diminishing Value rates, effective life, WDV) supporting tax claims. It is distinguished from: (a) `inventory_report` / `asset_register_proforma` — physical manifests that track item COUNTS, locations, and maintenance liability, with no tax-depreciation values; (b) `fitout_specification_schedule` / `scope_of_works_schedule` / `finishes_schedule` — design/construction specifications describing physical works, paint codes, and aesthetics rather than tax life and acquisition cost; (c) `works_cost_summary` / `works_contribution_worksheet` — landlord-tenant cost reconciliation worksheets that record the contribution quantum but do not partition assets into Div 40/43 or assign tax effective lives. The discriminating diagnostic is the presence of per-asset tax-life and depreciation-rate fields (Division 40/43, Prime Cost/Diminishing Value, WDV) authored by a third-party Quantity Surveyor."\n}'
  }

<Details summary={"documentation_authority_letter — Documentation Authority Letter"}>

  title={"documentation_authority_letter — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "documentation_authority_letter",\n  "type_name": "Documentation Authority Letter",\n  "description": "A formal commercial letter or administrative instruction issued by a party (typically the tenant or lessor / landlord) to their solicitor or to the counterparty\'s legal counsel, authorising the manual insertion of missing non-material details — such as final execution dates, title or folio references, lot or plan numbers, dealing references, or subdivision plans — into already-executed land-registry forms or deeds prior to official registration. Provides the legal permission an agent needs to complete or amend the physical text of an executed instrument without requiring re-execution by the parties, and operates as a pre-registration gatekeeper that carries instruction-specific metadata (authorising entity, target instrument number, and the precise details permitted for insertion) used to track document-completion workflows and avoid registry re-execution.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Includes Authorities to Complete, Insert-Details Authorisations, Legal Authority Letters, and formal letters of authority instructing solicitors (or counterparties\' counsel) to manually insert administrative details — execution dates, title or folio references, dealing numbers, subdivision plan numbers — into executed registry forms (e.g. NSW Form 07VL, QLD Form 13 Amendment) and deeds prior to lodgement. Also encompasses post-execution authorisations directed at lodging documents with a government registry on the principal\'s behalf.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Authorising entity (Tenant "deed_of_variation",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "post_execution_completion_authorisation",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the deed of variation requires post-execution "applicability_condition": "When the covering letter accompanies delivery or return of a bank-guarantee instrument."\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "deed_of_surrender",\n }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `operational_correspondence` (general administrative / lifecycle correspondence between parties): a documentation_authority_letter is a narrow, unilateral, client-to-lawyer permission to alter or lodge a specific named instrument and carries instruction-specific metadata (target instrument number, specific permitted insertions); operational_correspondence is the broad bilateral coordination layer (rate-card updates, billing instructions, fitout queries, informal notices) without instrument-completion-authority semantics. Also distinct from a solicitor\'s certification letter (lawyer-to-client assurance of document accuracy — opposite direction of authority flow), from a `land_registry_form` itself (the substantive registrable instrument being completed, not the authorisation to complete it), and from a `land_registry_correction_form` (a reactive statutory declaration lodged by the solicitor to fix a registered error, rather than a proactive client permission to insert missing detail pre-registration)."\n}'

It serves as the platform-generated, non-operative forensic record of electronic execution — independent of, but typically physically appended as terminal pages to, the operative deed it authenticates — providing the evidentiary metadata required to verify signatory identity, timing, and process integrity under the Electronic Transactions Acts.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_independent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers DocuSign Certificates of Completion, Adobe Acrobat Sign Final Audit Reports, Dropbox Sign Audit Trail Certificates, and generic Electronic Signature Audit Logs / Signing Summary Reports produced by other e-signature platforms. It defines the notice period, the effective break window(s), the triggers (fixed-date break, performance thresholds such as sales-to-rent or turnover floors, landlord redevelopment / demolition, kiosk-to-inline relocation bridges, or area-deficiency), the surrender sum / break fee, and the conditions precedent for an effective exercise (e.g. no unremedied default, make-good completion, vacant possession).",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_dependent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers fixed mid-term break options, performance-based termination (sales / turnover thresholds), landlord redevelopment or demolition breaks, short-term relocation-bridge terminations (e.g. kiosk-to-inline), area-deficiency termination rights, and surrender / break-fee variants. Spans clauses embedded in commercial and retail leases, retrofit insertions via variation tables, and early-stage forms in heads of agreement.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Break / termination triggers (fixed date window, sales-or-turnover threshold, redevelopment notice, relocation, area deficiency); notice period length (typically 3–12 months); effective termination date or window; surrender sum / break fee amount and calculation basis; conditions precedent (no unremedied default, vacant possession, make-good completion); and any associated surrender documentation requirements.",\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `surrender_of_lease` / deed of surrender: an early termination provision is a unilateral contractual OPTION pre-negotiated and embedded inside the lease, whereas a surrender deed is a separate, mutual, post-hoc bipartite instrument that actually executes the termination and extinguishes the leasehold estate. Distinguished from an expiry-obligations / make-good schedule: this concept defines the RIGHT TO EXIT before expiry; an expiry-obligations schedule defines the RESTORATION ACTIONS required whenever the lease ends (irrespective of how it ends). annexed surveyor-certified plan to definitively establish the spatial extent of the granted easement — the right-of-way track, width, coordinates, and (for volumetric easements) vertical limits of the `lease_agreement` (and its sub-types such as commercial_office_lease_agreement, retail_lease_agreement, industrial_lease_agreement): the easement grants a specific non-exclusive right of use (access, loading, drainage, utilities) over a defined area for the benefit of a dominant tenement, whereas a lease grants exclusive possession of a demised premises for a fixed term and creates a landlord-tenant relationship. Distinguished from a personal licence (e.g. car_park_licence_agreement, storage_licence_agreement): the easement is a registrable property interest that runs with the land and binds future owners of the servient tenement, whereas a licence is a personal contractual right that does not create an estate or interest in land. Distinguished from `building_management_statement`: an easement is a bilateral grant of a specific right-of-use between one dominant and one servient tenement (often between neighbours), whereas a BMS is a comprehensive multi-lot registrable governance instrument coordinating reciprocal easements, voting structures, and proportional cost-apportionment across all volumetric lot owners of a complex — both are registrable instruments coordinating multi-owner relationships, but the BMS operates at building/complex scale with a management group structure while the easement operates at the single bilateral right-of-use scale."\n}'

ECO Incident Report Form is the retrospective post-event qualitative debrief whose distinctive surface is the \'what worked\' / \'needs improving\' partition, post-incident start/complete timings, and improvement-action recommendations submitted to the EPC for procedural review. It is the master energy-procurement instrument for the asset, specifying National Metering Identifiers (NMIs) or Meter Installation Reference Numbers (MIRNs) for the supplied site, multi-tier energy rates (peak/off-peak), target consumption levels (kWh p.a.), service charges, and environmental product charges (e.g., VEEC, LREC) used to satisfy state and federal energy-efficiency obligations. Variants differ in the commodity supplied (electricity vs gas) and therefore in the meter-identifier scheme (NMI for electricity, MIRN for gas) and consumption units (kWh vs MJ), but the core contract spine — retailer, customer, supply period, rates schedule, target consumption, environmental product charges — is invariant.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Retailer details; customer entity / account name; site / supply address; National Metering Identifier (NMI) and/or Meter Installation Reference Number (MIRN); supply period (start and end dates); target consumption (kWh p.a.); peak and off-peak energy rates; service charges; and environmental certificate prices (e.g., VEEC, LREC).",\n  "relationship_roles": [],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `service_contract`, which procures labour and maintenance services from a contractor for a fee rather than the sale of a consumable commodity; an electricity sale agreement is the sale of a metered energy commodity (kWh / MJ) at agreed peak/off-peak rates. Distinct from `utility_bill`, which is the periodic third-party tax invoice that demands payment for actual metered consumption under the rates this agreement establishes — the electricity sale agreement is the master pricing-framework contract; the utility bill is the recurring point-of-consumption invoice issued against it."\n}'

It graphically maps the physical distribution of a building\'s active fire-safety infrastructure — fire detection zones, smoke compartments, smoke-exhaust-fan control zones, sprinkler valves and heads, fire indicator panels (FIPs), brigade boosters, pump rooms, and water tanks — to assist emergency services, facility managers, and certifying technicians during fire events, audits, and system maintenance. Typically displayed wall-mounted adjacent to fire indicator panels or valve rooms in accordance with AS 2118.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "context_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Encompasses Sprinkler Block Plans (AS 2118-compliant suppression-zone maps), Fire Alarm Location Diagrams, FIP zone maps, smoke-exhaust-fan zone logic tables, and combined Fire/Sprinkler block plans. "extractable_information_summary": "Building identifier / address; consultant or fire-engineer details; design standard (e.g. AS 2118.1, AS 1670); hazard classification (e.g. Ordinary Hazard Group 3 / water-tank capacities; sprinkler hardware legend; smoke-exhaust-fan activation logic; and area-of-operation / design-density parameters.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "compliance_spatial_evidence",\n      "relationship_type": "provides_evidence_for",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "purpose_description": "Provides the certified, wall-mounted spatial proof of sprinkler / detector / smoke-exhaust zone coverage that the annual statutory fire-safety attestation requires as physical evidence of system layout.",\n head-by-head positions, pipe sizing, hanger details, and design-density tables for a specific floor or tenancy — embedded in an as-built or architectural drawing set) by being a building-wide, free-standing tactical zone map of system-level hardware locations rather than a localised installation drawing. Distinguished from `fire_system_flow_test_report` (a quantitative hydraulic test report charting measured flow / pressure against design Duty or Hazard curves to certify water-supply adequacy) by being a graphical spatial map rather than empirical performance data — the block plan documents where the suppression infrastructure is; the flow test report documents how well it performs. Distinguished from `fire_safety_schedule` (a textual statutory inventory of essential safety measures × performance standards × inspection frequencies issued by a building surveyor) by being a graphical engineering diagram of zones and hardware locations rather than a tabular regulatory manifest. Distinguished from evacuation diagrams (egress paths for civilian occupants) by being targeted at fire-brigade first-responders and certifying technicians, not building occupants. Distinguished from cadastral / survey plans by mapping fire-system zones rather than tenure or property boundaries."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

Distinguished from `fire_safety_audit_report` (Phase 1 type_id `fire_safety_audit_report`): the FER is a forward-looking engineering design analysis prepared by an accredited fire safety engineer to justify a building\'s alternative-solution design; the audit report is a retrospective regulatory review prepared by a Building Regulation Consultant (\'Statement of Facts\', Section 80A review) that audits a building\'s existing statutory fire-safety paperwork baseline and recommends FSS reissue or consolidation — it does not perform fire dynamics modelling and does not author new performance solutions."\n}'

<Json
  title={"fire_safety_audit_report — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "fire_safety_audit_report",\n  "type_name": "Fire Safety Audit & Schedule Review Report",\n  "description": "A professional building-regulation review document (frequently titled \'Statement of Facts\', \'Compliance Review\', or \'Review of Fire Safety Measures\') prepared by an accredited Building Regulation Consultant. It synthesises a building\'s construction history across multiple regulatory eras (e.g. Ordinance 70 through NCC), identifies errors, omissions, performance-solution gaps, and fragmentation in existing statutory fire safety records, and provides a consolidated evidence base together with formal recommendations enabling a local authority to reissue or update a whole-of-building Fire Safety Schedule — most commonly under NSW Section 80A of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "context_wide",\n  "variant_coverage": "Encompasses Fire Safety Audit Reports, Schedule Review Reports, building-regulation \'Statement of Facts\' documents, Compliance Review Reports (administrative reviews of historical building records and compliance rectifications), and Section 80A consultancy reviews aimed at reissuing or consolidating whole-of-building Fire Safety Schedules.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Property/building address; preparing Building Regulation Consultant name and accreditation number; client/owner details; statutory purpose (e.g. Section 80A reissue); construction history timeline with DA/CC approvals across regulatory eras (Ordinance 70 → BCA → NCC); area/level partitioning (e.g. Areas A–E); summary of existing performance solutions (FER numbers); list of fragmented legacy schedules; identified errors, omissions and non-compliances in current Fire Safety Schedules and Annual Fire Safety Statements; and prioritised remediation/consolidation recommendations for schedule reissue.",\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `fire_safety_schedule` (the surveyor-issued tabular inventory of essential safety measures with reference standards and inspection frequencies — the \'what\' the audit report reviews and recommends corrections to) and from `annual_fire_safety_statement` (the owner-issued annual statutory declaration that the schedule\'s measures have been assessed and perform to standard — the \'done\' attestation the audit report retrospectively reviews for errors and omissions). Also distinguished from `fire_engineering_report`, which provides the engineering design justification for an alternative performance solution feeding INTO the schedule, whereas the audit report retrospectively diagnoses and recommends consolidation of the existing schedule and statement records themselves.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "fire_safety_schedule_audit",\n      "relationship_type": "audits",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Retrospectively audits one or more existing fire safety schedules, identifies errors, omissions and fragmentation across regulatory eras, and recommends consolidation or reissue of a corrected whole-of-building schedule (typically under NSW Section 80A).",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "fire_safety_schedule",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "historical_audit_basis",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      "role_id": "annual_fire_safety_statement_audit",\n      "relationship_type": "audits",\n      "necessity": "expected",\n      "purpose_description": "Reviews historical Annual Fire Safety Statements (AFSS) / Annual Essential Safety Measures Reports (AESMR) for the building, identifies administrative errors and omissions in the declared compliance evidence, and incorporates those findings into the consolidated recommendation set delivered to the local authority.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "annual_fire_safety_statement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "compliance_audit_review",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": []\n}'

Office-only tenancies typically omit the schedule.",\n      "containment_description": "A specialised technical engineering schedule defining slab/roof weight capacities, annexed to (and physically bound within) the master lease for an industrial or logistics facility."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `design_brief` (which every SE run cites as the closest sibling) in scope, posture, and consumer: a `floor_loading_schedule` is a concise, narrow-purpose operational reference enumerating only structural weight tolerances (slab UDL, axle/post loads, roof live loads, zone capacities) for tenant compliance during occupancy; a `design_brief` is a comprehensive, multi-disciplinary construction specification manual covering architectural, civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, fire-services, and sustainability requirements for the developer to deliver. The two artefacts overlap only on slab loading parameters, and the floor loading schedule\'s tabular weight-limits payload is a small, sharply-typed subset of the design brief\'s full engineering specification. <Details summary={"franchise_notification_letter — Franchise Notification Letter"}>

<Json
  title={"franchise_notification_letter — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "franchise_notification_letter",\n  "type_name": "Franchise Notification Letter",\n  "description": "A formal written communication from a master/corporate tenant group notifying a landlord that an approved franchisee partner will occupy the premises under licence. It serves as a procedural notice issued under specific lease variation/covenant clauses that permit franchisee occupation without requiring formal landlord consent, providing the franchisee\'s legal entity details (name, ABN/ACN), director names, registered address, premises identifier, effective commencement date, and the lease clause being relied upon. The master tenant remains the legal tenant; the franchisee occupies as a site-level operator under licence.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Variants are minor: all instances notify a single landlord about a single premises and identify one incoming franchisee operator. Observed variation is in (a) the legal-identity granularity provided for the franchisee (entity name + ABN/ACN + directors vs. entity + directors only), (b) whether the cited authorising clause is framed as a consent-waiver variation, a sub-licensing variation, or a permitted-franchisee clause, and (c) the framing of the originator (master tenant group vs. franchisor-tenant). The functional shape — one tenant notifies one landlord of one franchisee taking site occupation under a pre-existing lease right — is invariant.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Master/corporate tenant name; incoming franchisee entity name with ABN/ACN; franchisee director name(s); trade name; registered address; premises identifier (shop / site / address); effective date of franchisee occupation; and the specific lease clause reference being relied upon (e.g. permitted-franchisee, sub-licensing variation, or consent-waiver clause).",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "franchisee_occupation_notice",\n      "relationship_type": "notifies",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Formally notifies the landlord that an approved franchisee will commence site-level occupation of the premises under licence, satisfying the procedural notice obligation in the lease\'s franchisee-occupation / sub-licensing / permitted-franchisee covenant and identifying the incoming franchisee entity, directors, registered address, effective commencement date and the specific lease clause being relied upon.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "corporate_change_notification",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `consent_request_letter` because this instrument is a unilateral notification of an action already permitted by the lease (no landlord approval required — the lease\'s covenant pre-authorises franchisee occupation and merely requires the tenant to notify), whereas a consent request letter actively petitions the landlord for permission to undertake a dealing that requires consent. Distinguished from `deed_of_assignment` (and other tenure-transfer instruments) because this notice only updates the identity of the site-level operator (franchisee) under licence while the master tenant remains the legal tenant with continuing primary liability — no leasehold interest is transferred. Distinguished from `change_of_control_notice` because the legal tenant entity is unchanged; only the franchisee operating the site changes. Distinguished from `legal_succession_notice` (specifically its operator-substitution variant) because this instrument notifies the landlord of an incoming franchisee commencing site-level occupation for the first time under a pre-authorised franchisee-occupation / sub-licensing / permitted-franchisee covenant — there is no outgoing operator being replaced and no predecessor→successor entity transition. Route a document here when an approved franchisee first takes occupation under a cited lease clause; route it to `legal_succession_notice` when an existing operator of record at the premises is replaced by a successor operator (one franchise partner succeeding another)."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

</Details>

<Details summary={"handover_notice — Handover Notice"}>

<Json
  title={"handover_notice — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "handover_notice",\n  "type_name": "Handover Notice",\n  "description": "A formal administrative communication (typically a single-page notice or letter) issued by a landlord, developer, or their agent to a tenant specifying, confirming, or revising the date on which a premises is physically delivered for tenant fit-out. It operationalises the governing pre-occupancy contract by locking in the handover date, triggering the commencement of the fit-out period and rent-free window, coordinating delivery of prerequisite documents (e.g. certificates of currency, bank guarantees), and gating the release of staged incentive milestone payments.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers \'Notice of Revised Handover Date\', \'Handover Notification Letter\', and \'Fit-out Commencement Notice\' variants. Issued by landlords, developers, or their managing agents; typically targets a specific premises identifier (e.g. shop number) within a development. Substantive variant axis is whether the notice operates under an upstream pre-occupancy contract (Agreement to Lease) or directly under an already-executed lease without an intermediate AFL.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Lessor and lessee identities; premises identifier (e.g. shop number such as \'Shop T12\'); actual or revised handover date; rent commencement date; fit-out period duration; list of outstanding prerequisite documents (certificates of currency, bank guarantees, insurance policies); staged milestone-linked incentive payment breakdown (e.g. 50/45/5 split tied to handover gates); and reference to the governing agreement clause being operationalised (e.g. \'Clause 4 of the Agreement\').",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "handover_date_notification",\n      "relationship_type": "notifies",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Formally communicates the exact or revised date on which the premises is physically delivered to the tenant to commence fit-out, thereby triggering the fit-out period, rent commencement window, and staged incentive payment milestones defined in the governing pre-occupancy contract or lease.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "agreement_to_lease",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "milestone_event_notifications",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the tenancy is preceded by a pre-commencement development phase governed by an Agreement to Lease.",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "tenancy_lifecycle_notification",\n          "applicability_condition": "When the handover occurs directly under the lease agreement terms without an intermediate Agreement to Lease.",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `agreement_to_lease`: the AFL is the bilateral governing contract establishing the entire pre-occupancy framework (Sunset Dates, Practical Completion, fit-out contributions, incentive amounts in principle), whereas the handover notice is a unilateral single-page temporal trigger that operationalises a specific date within that pre-established framework. Distinguished from `lease_agreement`: the lease defines the leasehold estate and ongoing tenancy obligations, whereas the handover notice marks a single point-in-time event within the tenancy\'s setup phase. Distinguished from physical handover-inspection artefacts (e.g. handover protocols / defect checklists / condition reports): the handover notice carries date, prerequisite-document, and payment-milestone metadata rather than physical-condition observations of the premises. Distinguished from fit-out briefs and design specifications: the handover notice coordinates the timing of physical delivery rather than specifying the physical works content."\n}'

Distinguished from `condition_report` — the condition report is a third-party-surveyor evidentiary baseline (qualitative element-level ratings, photographic register, FF&E inventory) used for make-good / dilapidation / yield-up enforcement at lease commencement, handover, or surrender, whereas the handover_protocol is narrower in scope: a construction-handover joint inspection focused on services certifications, utility meter baselines, and an outstanding-defects (Snag) list under the AFL. Distinguished from `fitout_brief` — the fit-out brief is a prospective technical specification / scope-of-works partitioning landlord-vs-tenant responsibilities for works to be done, whereas the handover_protocol is a terminal, point-in-time record verifying what was delivered."\n}'

    '{\n  "type_id": "incentive_adjustment_deed",\n  "type_name": "Incentive Adjustment Deed",\n  "description": "A formal commercial agreement — frequently manifesting as a letter-deed or side agreement — executed post-lease inception by the landlord and tenant to modify the application, conversion, or timing of an existing financial incentive previously granted under an incentive deed, fit-out deed, or agreement for lease. Typical operative content reallocates unspent construction-phase provisional sums into temporal rent-free periods or rent credits using an agreed time-value discount rate, reprogrammes rent-reduction schedules, adds supplementary works allowances, or alters landlord works obligations post-commencement. The same instrument is also used to novate the original incentive arrangement to a new party (for example following assignment or a change of ownership), substituting incoming for outgoing parties on the original incentive covenants.",\n  "standalone_classification": "standalone",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers (a) formal Deeds of Variation of an Incentive Deed or Fit-out Deed, (b) Incentive Application / Incentive Adjustment Agreements, (c) side letters formally shifting rent-credit or rent-free schedules, (d) deeds adding or revising fitout/works allowances mid-project or concurrently with a lease extension, and (e) novation-style variations that replace one of the original parties to the incentive arrangement (e.g. following assignment or change of ownership).",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Reference to the original incentive deed / fit-out deed / agreement for lease being varied; variation/execution date; parties (including incoming and outgoing party identities where the instrument also novates); unspent provisional sum balance being reallocated; converted rent-free period duration and/or rent-credit amounts; applied time-value discount rate used for the cash-to-rent-free conversion; revised rent-reduction schedule; supplementary or revised works allowances and updated work descriptions; amortisation / abatement start date.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "incentive_terms_modification",\n      "relationship_type": "varies",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Directly amends the commercial terms of an existing incentive arrangement — substituting new funding dates, reallocating unspent provisional sums into rent-free periods or rent credits via a time-value discount rate, reprogramming rent-reduction schedules, adding or revising works allowances, or novating the original incentive to a new party.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "incentive_and_fitout_deed",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "incentive_terms_modification",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "agreement_to_lease",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "incentive_modification",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinct from `incentive_and_fitout_deed` — that concept establishes the original grant (baseline incentive amount, fit-out contribution caps, rent-free dates, clawback formulas at inception); this concept varies the application, conversion, or timing of an already-granted incentive after lease inception. Distinct from `incentive_side_letter` — the side letter operationalises the per-category split of a previously agreed incentive pool (fitout vs rent-abatement vs make-good allocations and their commencement dates) without amending the size or rules of the pool itself; this concept amends the size, schedule, or party identity of the underlying grant. Distinct from `incentive_provision` — that concept is the embedded-clause counterpart of the standalone incentive deed (clauses physically embedded inside a lease/sublease/AFL body); this concept is a physically free-standing variation instrument, not a clausal section. Distinct from a general `deed_of_variation` of a lease — a lease variation alters ongoing possessory terms (term, base rent, premises); this concept exclusively varies the financial-inducement/works-allowance package."\n}'
  }
  collapsedDepth={1}
/>

</Details>

Distinguished from `incentive_adjustment_deed` (and its older labels incentive_variation_agreement, variation_of_incentive_deed), which legally amends the size, conversion rate, timing rules, or party identities of the underlying incentive pool — this instrument does NOT change the pool itself, it only operationalises the per-category split and effective dates within an unchanged pool (D2 PATCH addendum). Distinguished from `incentive_confirmation_deed` (Deed of Confirmation of Works), which is a post-execution sign-off that the landlord\'s construction obligations have been technically completed and the Scope of Works / handover dates locked in — that instrument confirms works completion; this instrument fixes the financial allocation. It defines the certifier\'s scope of services, fiduciary duty of independence, professional indemnity insurance requirements, fee structure, reporting frequency, and decision-making powers — notably certifying Practical Completion, assessing variations, determining extensions of time (EOT), preparing defects lists, and where applicable validating bespoke milestones such as temperature drawdown.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_independent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Covers tripartite Independent Certifier Deeds and pro-forma certifier templates embedded as schedules within Agreements for/to Lease, as well as standalone tripartite certifier deeds delivered separately for commercial, industrial and build-to-suit developments. Naming variants include \'Independent Certifier Deed\' and \'Certifier\'s Deed\'.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Tripartite parties (Developer/Principal/Landlord, Tenant, Consultant/Certifier); nominated key personnel for the certifier; reference to the parent Agreement for/to Lease and project description; scope of certification services (Practical Completion, EOT determinations, defects rectification, variation review, milestone-specific items such as temperature drawdown); Professional Indemnity (PI) insurance limit (e.g. $10M, $15M); consultant fee structure and fee caps; reporting frequency (e.g. monthly); dispute-resolution / arbitration powers; and project completion dates.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "progress_adjudication_appointment",\n      "relationship_type": "supplements",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Appoints an independent third-party certifier to impartially adjudicate construction progress under the parent Agreement for/to Lease — certifying Practical Completion, assessing variations and extensions of time, and preparing defects lists — so that the lease-commencement-trigger event is determined by an independent expert rather than by either deal-side party.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "agreement_to_lease",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "certifier_appointment"\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": [\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "agreement_to_lease",\n      "containment_certainty": "definitive",\n      "expected_presence": "conditional",\n      "containment_description": "Typically annexed as a structural schedule or pro-forma template deed inside an Agreement for/to Lease, binding the parties to execute the certifier\'s appointment as a condition of (or alongside) the development works package. When physically embedded the deed remains functionally independent — it constitutes a separate tripartite contract regarding the certifier\'s duties even though it is structurally housed as an AFL schedule. A standalone variant (deed delivered as a physically separate tripartite contract) is also observed and is captured in variant_coverage.",\n      "condition": "When the AFL physically annexes the certifier appointment as an execution-ready schedule/deed; the dominant template only names the certifier and defers execution."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `practical_completion_report` (and related technical_inspection_report-type outputs) because the deed is the contractual *appointment* of the certifier — establishing their authority, fees, PI insurance and reporting duties — whereas the report is the technical *output* that the certifier subsequently produces under the deed\'s authority. Distinguished from `service_contract` because the deed is a tripartite construction-adjudication instrument with a fiduciary duty of impartiality between two principal parties, not a bilateral operational-services engagement (cleaning, maintenance, security). Distinguished from bilateral incentive or fitout deeds because the third-party certifier is a distinct contracting principal with independent legal duties, not merely a beneficiary or consultant nominee under a bilateral arrangement."\n}'

the certificate of currency is the outbound EVIDENCE issued by the tenant\'s insurer in response. Distinguished from `operational_correspondence`: the update request has a strict, single-purpose compliance-enforcement function (demand for updated insurance evidence), whereas the operational_correspondence umbrella covers heterogeneous operational communications (rate-card adjustments, bank-guarantee exchange letters, billing instructions, fitout queries, deal-approval forms, handover notices, informal variation letters, settlement offers, etc.). When the corpus-side document is unambiguously an insurance-compliance demand letter, prefer `insurance_update_request`; when it is a general operational/administrative letter not narrowly scoped to insurance evidence, prefer `operational_correspondence`. Distinguished from an insurer\'s renewal-billing / account-summary statement (see synthesis_escalations): a landlord-to-tenant compliance demand is in scope here; an insurer-to-policyholder billing statement is out of scope and belongs to a separate concept that the orchestrator should carve out."\n}'

Distinct from tenant-facing operational manuals (e.g., `building_users_guide`, `house_rules`, `lease_rules`) which address occupants/tenants rather than internal staff. Distinct from in-lease operational annexures (e.g., the building-services `management_procedures` annexure embedded in a lease) which are relationship-specific sub-components of a particular lease rather than corporate-wide SOPs. Distinct from corporate conduct/HR policies (e.g., `business_conduct_policy`, `corporate_policy_set`) which set behavioural standards rather than transactional workflows. Distinct from `execution_page`: this SOP provides the internal rules on HOW to sign/execute a document, whereas the execution_page is where the actual signature is physically placed on the executed instrument.",\n  "relationship_roles": [\n    {\n      "role_id": "administrative_workflow_governance",\n      "relationship_type": "governs",\n      "necessity": "required",\n      "purpose_description": "Defines the mandatory administrative workflow, sign-off layers, and limits-of-authority gates that internal transaction-handling artefacts (execution request forms and internal approval records) must conform to when staff route, approve, execute, and register leasing instruments.",\n      "acceptable_targets": [\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "document_execution_request_form",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "governed_by_internal_procedure",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        },\n        {\n          "target_type_id": "internal_approval_record",\n          "counterpart_role_id": "procedural_governance_compliance",\n          "parent_relationship_contexts": []\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  "containment_contexts": []\n}'

<Json
  title={"internet_service_agreement — production entry"}
  json={
    '{\n  "type_id": "internet_service_agreement",\n  "type_name": "Internet Service Agreement",\n  "description": "A formal agreement (often annexed to a commercial lease) governing the provision and ongoing delivery of managed high-speed fibre internet and WiFi services by a landlord to a tenant. It defines technical support levels, hardware specifications and quantities (e.g. WiFi access points, PoE switches), uptime service-level guarantees, recurring monthly connection and support charges, and the targeted activation date for the integrated technology infrastructure.",\n  "standalone_classification": "embedded_independent",\n  "document_scope": "relationship_specific",\n  "variant_coverage": "Includes embedded internet service provisions, managed fibre agreements (e.g. Fibre 500/500), and integrated \'Design Suite\' technology packages bundling WiFi access points, PoE switches, and uptime-graded support tiers.",\n  "extractable_information_summary": "Service type (e.g. Fibre 500/500); support level / tier; hardware manifest and counts (WiFi access points, PoE switches, other network equipment); uptime guarantees (typically 99.00%–99.95%); monthly connection and support charges; targeted activation date.",\n  "relationship_roles": [],\n  "containment_contexts": [\n    {\n      "parent_type_id": "lease_agreement",\n      "containment_certainty": "definitive",\n      "expected_presence": "optional",\n      "containment_description": "Structurally annexed to a commercial lease agreement as an IT-services / connectivity schedule covering managed fibre internet and WiFi delivery to the demised premises."\n    }\n  ],\n  "sibling_discriminators": "Distinguished from `service_contract` (the owner/property-manager to specialist-contractor master operational agreement for building-wide services such as cleaning, HVAC, security, fire, hydraulic, electrical, vertical transport): `service_contract` is a standalone, bilaterally executed commercial agreement between building owner and trade contractor governing portfolio- or building-level operational services for a fee, whereas `internet_service_agreement` is an embedded annexure to a specific tenant lease governing landlord-to-tenant managed connectivity (fibre + WiFi) with tenant-scoped hardware manifests, monthly charges, and uptime SLAs. The two also differ on standalone classification (`standalone` vs `embedded_independent`), parties (owner↔contractor vs landlord↔tenant), and scope vocabulary (building-wide trade services vs single-tenancy IT utility provision). Distinguished from incentive deeds because incentive deeds manage one-off capital setup and construction contributions, whereas an internet service agreement governs ongoing operational technology delivery and recurring monthly charges. Distinguished from `service_order`: an `internet_service_agreement` is an embedded_independent IT-services annexure bound INSIDE a host lease where the landlord IS the connectivity provider to its own tenant (tenant-scoped WiFi access-point / PoE-switch hardware manifest and counts, uptime SLA of 99.00%-99.95%, integrated \'Design Suite\' technology package, recurring monthly connection and support charges), whereas a `service_order` is a standalone, free-standing provider<->customer procurement order form (external carrier/provider name, customer legal name, site address, Mbps capacity, port configuration, setup / monthly recurring charges, contract term) that grants no interest in land and is not bound inside the lease. The shared fibre/internet product vocabulary is incidental: landlord-provided, lease-embedded managed connectivity routes here; standalone provider order forms route to `service_order`."\n}'
  }
